channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [10] Nematic and chiral superconductivity emerging within the loop-current phase in kagome metals
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Youichi Yamakawa, Hiroshi Kontani

Authors: Rina Tazai, Youichi Yamakawa, Hiroshi Kontani

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Directly addresses core research topics: kagome metals, AV3Sb5, nematicity, and loop currents.

Tags: #material:AV3Sb5 #topic:kagome #topic:nematicity #topic:loop-current

Abstract: The authors show that the loop-current in the normal state gives rise to nematic chiral d-wave superconductivity in AV3Sb5 kagome metals, further enhanced by bond order. For attractive pairing, weak impurity scattering suppresses the chiral state and restores a conventional s-wave phase, as observed experimentally.
